night-plum.note: Page ground and canvas floor, lifted by radial-gradient(120% 90% at 50% 0%, #241119 0%, #150A10 58%).

plum-raised.note: The only solid raised surface: the nav brush when paint mode is off.

hot-pink.note: The one action colour. Shipped as a gradient on filled controls: #FF67AC 0% -> #FF4D9D 55% -> #F02D85 100%.

pink-deep.note: Bottom stop of the pink gradient; also PALETTE[0], the wall's default paint colour.

ink-on-pink.note: Type colour on pink fills only. Never a background.

rose.note: Text-level accent: links, ghost labels, countdown chip, sheet icons.

rose-bright.note: The display-type colour. Pixel-face headings land here, not on pure white.

paper-pink.note: Body text. Pure #FFF appears only on crop handles, thumbnail backing and the custom-swatch border.

dim-mauve.note: Secondary text, unselected nav, captions; placeholders at 55% alpha.

mint-ok.note: Approved, live, saved, free space on the wall. Border variant at 0.35-0.5 alpha.

amber-warn.note: Pending, waiting, out of paint, offline. The most-used semantic colour, because pre-moderation makes most states waiting states. Its ink is #241300.

coral-danger.note: Rejected, invalid field, booked space. Never a destructive button fill.

glass.note: Resting fill of anything floating over the canvas. Alpha ladder rather than a tonal ramp: 0.58 glass, 0.82 glass-hard, 0.94 the @supports-not fallback.

glass-hard.note: For content that must stay readable at any canvas zoom: toasts and tooltips.

glass-border.note: The hairline light edge of every glass pill.

hairline.note: Dividers and quiet borders inside opaque surfaces.

hairline-strong.note: The edge of interactive objects: inputs, ghost buttons, cards that act.

display.purpose: Largest pixel-face moment: pack amounts and the InstaPay total. Nothing sets the pixel face above 15px.

headline.purpose: Sheet titles, preceded by an 18px pink icon, with 40px inline-end padding to clear the close button.

title.purpose: The S37 lockup, success headings, status-card headings.

action.purpose: Primary CTA label, pixel selection counter, step numerals, checkout total.

label.purpose: Field labels, chips, mini buttons, coordinates. Sub-steps at 7.5px and 7px exist for chips inside 20-26px pills.

nav-label.purpose: Bottom-nav doors only. The floor of the system; do not reuse elsewhere. Steps to 10px in Arabic.

body-small.purpose: The working size inside sheets: descriptions, list rows, toasts, checkout lines.

caption.purpose: Hints, fine print, timestamps, character counts — always on Dim Mauve.

input.purpose: All text fields and the stepper. 16px is a floor, not a preference: iOS zooms below it.

fonts.name: Press Start 2P
fonts.note: No Arabic glyphs — the reason --fp exists.

shadows.name: glass-lift
shadows.purpose: Every .glass pill and the zoom rail. The inset highlight is what makes the pill read as a lit edge.

shadows.name: pink-lift
shadows.purpose: The primary CTA. Removed entirely when disabled.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: Bottom sheet rising from the bottom edge on a phone.

shadows.name: dialog-lift
shadows.purpose: The same sheet once it becomes a centered dialog at 760px.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Input focus halo, paired with a hot-pink border shift.

shadows.name: swatch-ring
shadows.purpose: The selected paint swatch, paired with a white border and scale(1.12).

shadows.name: crop-scrim
shadows.purpose: A spread shadow used as a dimmer for everything outside the crop box.

motion.name: expo
motion.purpose: The one curve. Sheet entry, toast entry, dock hide, badge pop, success pop, every press transform.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.purpose: Toast arrival; exit translates up 8px at zero opacity over 300ms ease.

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: Scrim only. Linear easing is reserved for fades.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons and swatches. Presses are physical: translate or scale, never a colour swap.

motion.name: dock-hide
motion.purpose: The paint dock leaving when the app enters placement mode.

motion.name: shake
motion.purpose: Refusal feedback on the pixel counter. A refused action shakes; it does not change colour.

breakpoints.name: base
breakpoints.note: Mobile-first: the base stylesheet is a phone in one hand.

breakpoints.name: duo
breakpoints.note: Pre-order source image and preview go side by side.

breakpoints.name: dialog
breakpoints.note: Sheets become centered dialogs; auth two-column; packs three-across; minimap 84 -> 148px; dock centers at min(680px, 100% - 20px).

breakpoints.name: editor
breakpoints.note: Pre-order editor becomes a two-column workspace with its own scrolling form column.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.note: Sheet widths settle: 620 default / 1140 wide editor / 480 alerts-me-more.

breakpoints.name: landscape-short
breakpoints.note: Lockup drops its text, dock becomes one row at 74px, nav 56px with a 48px brush, coordinates hide.

material.name: liquid glass
material.value: background: rgba(28,14,22,0.58); backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(160%); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.14); box-shadow: 0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.38), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.09)
material.fallback: @supports not ((backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(1px))) { background: rgba(28,14,22,0.94) }
material.purpose: The single depth rule for anything floating over the wall. Sheets are opaque and layer tonally instead.

paintPalette.note: Content colours owned by app.js (PALETTE), not chrome. A seventeenth swatch is a conic-gradient door to the native colour picker.

narrative.northStar: The Lit Window on a Plum Night
narrative.overview:
The wall is the room; everything else is glass you look through to see it. A million pixels of other people's marks fill the phone from notch to home bar, and every control the app owns — the lockup, the countdown, the language toggle, the paint dock, the five-door nav — is a blurred, translucent, hairline-bordered pill floating on top of that artwork. Nothing is stacked above or below the canvas. There is no header band, no footer band, no letterboxed content well. Chrome is weather over the wall, not architecture around it.

The ground is a dark plum night (#150A10) with one warm radial lift toward the top of the canvas, so the surface never reads as flat black. Against it the system speaks in two registers: a rose family for everything that is merely text (#F5C4C1 into #FBE1DF), and one hot pink (#FF4D9D) reserved for the single thing you are meant to press. The pixel display face — Press Start 2P at 400, Cairo at 800 when the page speaks Arabic — never grows large; it lives from 6.5px to 15px and works as a label voice, while Figtree carries every real sentence at 12–16px. That inversion is the personality: the arcade voice is small and clipped, the human voice is bigger and softer.

Density is generous for thumbs and tight for pixels. Touch targets sit at 38–58px, sheets rise from the bottom edge on a phone and become centered dialogs at 760px, and every fixed offset carries a safe-area inset. Confirmed refusal: the category-default chrome sandwich — an opaque top bar over a scrolling content column over an opaque bottom bar — which shrinks the artwork to a window. That composition is not available in this system.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed live canvas; all chrome floats over it
Liquid glass as the single material: 20px blur, 160% saturation, hairline light border
Dark plum night ground with one hot-pink primary action per surface
Pixel display face used small (6.5–15px) as a label voice; Figtree used larger for prose
Pill-shaped floating controls, panel-radius sheets, zero square corners outside the canvas
Mobile-first, logical-property layout that mirrors whole for Arabic RTL
Sprite-only pixelarticons, always sized in px

rules.name: The One Loud Thing Rule
rules.body: Exactly one hot-pink filled control per surface. On the wall that is the raised brush; inside a sheet it is the single primary CTA. Everything else that wants attention gets rose text, a pink hairline, or a pink icon — never a second pink fill.

rules.name: The Two Palettes Rule
rules.body: Chrome colours and wall-paint colours are separate sets and do not borrow from each other. The only sanctioned crossing is #D81B60, which is both the deep stop of the chrome pink and the default paint colour.

rules.name: The Veil, Not Blackout Rule
rules.body: Sheet scrims are rgba(10, 4, 8, 0.30) with blur(2px). The wall stays alive and visible behind every overlay — a modal never turns the artwork off.

rules.name: The Small Pixel Rule
rules.body: The pixel display face never grows. It runs 6.5px to 15px and is always a label, a heading or a numeral — never a sentence, never a paragraph. Prose is Figtree, and Figtree is the larger of the two faces on screen.

rules.name: The Never Hardcode a Family Rule
rules.body: Every display moment goes through var(--fp) + var(--fp-w) and every body moment through var(--fb). Writing font-family: 'Press Start 2P' directly breaks Arabic silently, because Press Start 2P has no Arabic glyphs.

rules.name: The 16px Input Rule
rules.body: Text inputs are 16px, always. Anything smaller makes iOS Safari zoom the viewport on focus and the full-bleed canvas never recovers its framing.

rules.name: The Safe-Area Rule
rules.body: Every fixed edge offset is written as calc(<n>px + var(--sat|--sab|--sal|--sar)). The page renders under the notch on purpose (viewport-fit=cover); the insets are what keeps controls out from under it.

rules.name: The Logical Property Rule
rules.body: Shell layout uses logical properties only — inset-inline, padding-inline, margin-inline, text-align: start, border-inline-end. Setting dir="rtl" must mirror the whole shell with no extra CSS. The only physical offsets in the system are the eight crop handles, which are geometric positions on an image rather than layout.

rules.name: The Hidden Property Rule
rules.body: Every conditional element — sheets, error lines, badges, optional rows — toggles via the HTML hidden property, backed by [hidden] { display: none !important }. Do not invent .is-open / .d-none classes; the attribute is the state.

rules.name: The Glass-Over-Canvas Rule
rules.body: If it floats above the wall, it wears .glass. If it lives inside a sheet, it is a tonal surface with a hairline border. Never nest glass inside glass — the second blur has nothing left to blur.

rules.name: The Pink Glow Rule
rules.body: Coloured shadows belong to the primary action alone. Two elements carry a pink glow (the raised brush and the CTA); a third would flatten both.

rules.name: The Pill-or-Panel Rule
rules.body: Floating controls are pills; grouped content is a panel at 10 / 18 / 26px. There is no third shape and no square corner outside the canvas.

rules.name: The Sprite-Only Rule
rules.body: Every icon is <svg class="ic"><use href="#i-…"/></svg> from the generated pixelarticons sprite. New icons are added to the mapping in tools/make-icons.js and regenerated — never hand-drawn into the markup, and never sized in em/rem.

dos: Do keep the canvas full-bleed and float new chrome over it as a .glass pill positioned with position: fixed plus a safe-area inset.
Do give each surface exactly one hot-pink filled control (The One Loud Thing Rule); express every other emphasis as rose text, a pink icon, or a pink hairline.
Do write display type as font-family: var(--fp); font-weight: var(--fp-w) and add an Arabic size bump (html[lang="ar"] .thing { font-size: … }) whenever the Latin size is under 9px.
Do use logical properties for every offset, padding and alignment so dir="rtl" mirrors the shell for free.
Do toggle every conditional element with the hidden property, and keep error messages as pre-existing hidden elements rather than injected nodes.
Do pair every semantic colour with words — a pending row says "pending" and is amber; the colour is reinforcement, not the message.
Do size icons in px on a .ic override (12 / 16 / 18–22 / 26 / 44) and pull them from the inline sprite with <use>.
Do keep text inputs at 16px and touch targets at 38px or larger (44px for standalone controls).
Do keep behaviour in app.js — the page ships no inline script and no inline handlers.
donts: Don't build a chrome sandwich: no opaque top bar plus scrolling content column plus opaque bottom bar. Nothing may reduce the canvas to a letterboxed window.
Don't blur a .glass surface inside another .glass surface, and don't apply glass to content that lives inside a sheet — sheets are opaque and layer tonally.
Don't add a second pink-filled control, or a second coloured shadow, to a surface that already has one.
Don't set the pixel display face above 15px, or use it for a sentence. Prose is Figtree.
Don't hardcode 'Press Start 2P' or 'Figtree' anywhere — Arabic swaps both through custom properties and a hardcoded family renders tofu.
Don't use physical left / right / margin-left in shell layout; the RTL mirror depends on logical properties.
